scenarios.title: Renting an Apartment
scenarios.summary: Sam views a one-bedroom apartment and asks the landlord about utilities, the lease, references and repairs. It also has a short lease clause.

scenarios.canadaNoteZh: 租房规则(押金、租约、退租通知)各省差别很大。签约前一定要读完租约,不懂就问,并保留租约和所有收据的副本。
verify: Deposit rules differ by province (whether one is allowed, what it can be called). The text says only that a deposit may be asked for and that it should be in writing.
Renewal as month-to-month after a fixed lease is common but the rule differs by province.
Written notice to end a tenancy and its length differ by province and lease type. The text gives no length.
Landlords may ask for references and proof of income in many places, but some provinces limit what can be asked. The text keeps to the general case.
Heat and water included in rent is an example in the story, not a rule.
The lease excerpt is written for the story. It is not a real lease and must not be taken as the legal wording of any province.

segments.text: Sam is looking for a one-bedroom apartment. He has arranged a viewing, and the landlord, Ms. Patel, is showing him around.

lines.speaker: Ms. Patel
lines.text: Welcome, Sam. This is the unit I told you about. As you can see, the kitchen was renovated recently.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Wow, this is a big improvement over my last place. Is it all right if I have a look around?

lines.speaker: Ms. Patel
lines.text: Of course, take your time.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: It looks great, and there is plenty of natural light. Could you tell me what the rent includes?

lines.speaker: Ms. Patel
lines.text: Heat and water are included. The other utilities, electricity and internet, are yours to pay, and you would set up those accounts in your own name.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: That is good to know. What kind of lease is it? Is it for a fixed term?

lines.speaker: Ms. Patel
lines.text: Yes, it is a one-year lease. After that, it can continue month to month if we both agree.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: I see. Do you ask for a deposit?

lines.speaker: Ms. Patel
lines.text: I do, before you move in. I will put the details in writing, and you will get a receipt for everything you pay.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Understood. What do you need from me to apply?

lines.speaker: Ms. Patel
lines.text: A rental application, proof of income such as a recent pay stub or a letter from your employer, and two references. A previous landlord is the best reference.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: I have lived in my current place for three years, so my landlord can speak for me. What about pets? I have a small cat.

lines.speaker: Ms. Patel
lines.text: Cats are fine, but please let me know so I can add it to the lease. Smoking is not allowed anywhere in the building.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: That is not a problem for me. If something breaks, like the stove, who should I contact?

lines.speaker: Ms. Patel
lines.text: Contact me or the building manager. We fix small problems within a few days, and emergencies, such as a flood, right away.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Would you recommend tenant insurance?

lines.speaker: Ms. Patel
lines.text: Strongly. My insurance covers the building, not your belongings, and many landlords now ask tenants to have it.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: One last question. If I decide to move out, how much notice do I have to give?

lines.speaker: Ms. Patel
lines.text: You must give written notice. The rules depend on the type of lease, so I will explain them before you sign anything.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Thank you. I would like to apply.

lines.speaker: Ms. Patel
lines.text: Wonderful. Send me your documents by the end of the week, and I will give you my decision within a few days. Just a heads up: good units go fast around here.

segments.text: From the lease: The tenant agrees to pay the rent on or before the first day of each month. The tenant shall keep the unit clean and shall not make changes to it without the landlord's written consent. The landlord shall carry out repairs within a reasonable time after being notified. A tenant who wishes to end the tenancy must give written notice as required by law.

Tip: Before you sign a lease, read it carefully and ask about anything you do not understand. Keep a copy of the lease and every receipt. On moving day, take photos of the apartment, so you can show its condition later.

scenarios.summary: Amira meets a banker to open a chequing account and learns about fees, a debit card and online banking. It also has a short fee notice.

scenarios.canadaNoteZh: 加拿大的银行不会通过电话、短信或邮件向你索要密码或 PIN。收到这类消息就是诈骗,不要回复。
verify: Which identification a bank accepts, and how many pieces, differs by bank. The text says only that ID is needed.
Whether a bank asks for a SIN when opening an account (it is usually requested for tax reporting on interest) and what is possible without one. The text does not mention it.
Newcomer packages and fee waivers differ by bank and change over time. The text says only that some accounts have a monthly fee that can be avoided in some cases.
Interac e-Transfer is widely used, but daily limits and fees differ by bank. The text gives no numbers.
Overdraft protection and its charges differ by bank.

The fee notice is written for the story and is not the wording of any real bank. Whether a customer may close an account without penalty after a fee change depends on the bank and the rules; check before relying on it.

segments.text: Amira has a job offer and needs a bank account for her pay. She has come to a bank branch and is speaking with a banker, Mr. Lee.

lines.speaker: Mr. Lee
lines.text: Good morning. How can I help you today?

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.text: Hello. I would like to open a bank account. I will start a new job soon, and I want my pay to go straight into the account.

lines.speaker: Mr. Lee
lines.text: Sure thing. Have a seat, and I will get you set up.

lines.speaker: Mr. Lee
lines.text: Congratulations. That is called direct deposit, and it is easy to set up. Do you have identification with you?

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.text: Yes, I brought my passport and a document with my home address.

lines.speaker: Mr. Lee
lines.text: Perfect. Most people start with a chequing account, which you use for everyday spending. You can also open a savings account, which pays interest on the money you keep in it.

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.text: What is the difference in practice?

lines.speaker: Mr. Lee
lines.text: With chequing, you can pay bills, use your debit card and send money to other people. A savings account is better for money you do not plan to spend soon.

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.text: Is there a monthly fee?

lines.speaker: Mr. Lee
lines.text: Some chequing accounts have one. You can often avoid it by keeping a minimum balance. I will show you the options and explain the details on paper, so you can compare them.

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.text: Thank you. Will I get a debit card?

lines.speaker: Mr. Lee
lines.text: Yes. You will choose a PIN, a secret number that you must never share with anyone, even someone from the bank. You can tap the card in most stores.

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.text: What if I spend more money than I have in the account?

lines.speaker: Mr. Lee
lines.text: That is called an overdraft, and the bank may charge you for it. Some accounts have overdraft protection. I suggest you check your balance often.

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.text: Can I do that online?

lines.speaker: Mr. Lee
lines.text: Of course. We will set up online banking and a mobile app. You can see your statements, pay bills and send an e-transfer to friends.

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.text: That sounds convenient. Is it safe?

lines.speaker: Mr. Lee
lines.text: Yes, if you are careful. Use a strong password and never click a link in a message that asks for your banking details. We will never ask for your password by phone or e-mail.

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.text: Good to know. I would like to open the chequing account today.

lines.speaker: Mr. Lee
lines.text: Wonderful. Let me review the agreement with you, and then we can begin.

segments.text: Notice: Changes to your account fees. From time to time we may change the fees on your account. We will tell you in writing before a change is due to take effect. If you do not agree to the change, you may close your account without penalty. Please read this notice carefully and keep it for your records.
Tip: Ask the bank to explain every fee before you agree. Check your statement every month, and report anything you do not recognize right away.

segments.text: Daniel's daughter Lina is in grade five. Tonight is the parent-teacher meeting, and Daniel is talking with Lina's teacher, Ms. Roberts.

lines.speaker: Ms. Roberts
lines.text: Thank you for coming, Mr. Haddad. Lina is a pleasure to have in my class.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: I am glad to hear that. We read her report card together last week, but I have a few questions.

lines.speaker: Ms. Roberts
lines.text: Of course. Let me start with her strengths. She reads well, she participates in discussions, and she is kind to the other students.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: That is wonderful. At home she reads before bed every night.

lines.speaker: Ms. Roberts
lines.text: Please do not worry. She is doing fine overall, and I will keep an eye on how she does with word problems.

lines.speaker: Ms. Roberts
lines.text: It shows. Her writing is improving too. The area where she tends to struggle a little is math, especially word problems.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Yes, I noticed that she gets frustrated with her math homework. Sometimes she says she does not understand the question.

lines.speaker: Ms. Roberts
lines.text: That is common for students who are learning English as well. The math itself is not too difficult for her. The language in the problems is the challenge.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: What can we do at home to help?

lines.speaker: Ms. Roberts
lines.text: Ask her to explain the problem in her own words before she solves it. If she can say it in Arabic first, that is perfectly fine, and then practise the English words. Reading the problems aloud also helps.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: We can do that. Is there any extra help at school?

lines.speaker: Ms. Roberts
lines.text: There is a homework club after school, and I can ask the support teacher to work with her in small groups. I will send you the details.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: That would be very helpful. How can I reach you if I have a concern?

lines.speaker: Ms. Roberts
lines.text: You can write to me in her agenda or send me an e-mail. I usually reply within a couple of days. If it is urgent, please call the school office.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Thank you. One more thing: if I do not understand something at a meeting, may I ask for an interpreter?

lines.speaker: Ms. Roberts
lines.text: Absolutely. Please tell the school office in advance and they will see what they can arrange.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: I appreciate it. We will work on the math together.

lines.speaker: Ms. Roberts
lines.text: Wonderful. Let us check in again in a few weeks and see how she is progressing.

segments.text: From the school newsletter: Parent-teacher interviews will take place next week. Please sign up for a time slot using the form sent home with your child. If you need an interpreter or have any questions, contact the school office.
Tip: Before the meeting, write down two or three questions. Ask the teacher for examples of the child's work, and ask what you can do at home. Teachers like to hear from parents.

segments.text: Omar is interviewing for a customer service position at a large store. The manager, Ms. Chen, welcomes him into her office.

lines.speaker: Ms. Chen
lines.text: Hello, Omar. Thank you for coming. Please have a seat. Could you start by telling me a little about yourself?

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: Thank you for meeting me. I moved to Canada last year. In my home country I worked for four years in a mobile phone shop, where I helped customers choose plans and fixed simple problems. Since I arrived, I have also volunteered at a community centre.

lines.speaker: Ms. Chen
lines.text: That sounds relevant. What would you say is your greatest strength?

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: I stay calm with upset customers. I listen first, repeat the problem to make sure I understand, and then look for a solution.

lines.speaker: Ms. Chen
lines.text: Can you give me an example?

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: Certainly. Once, a customer was angry because his phone had been repaired twice and still did not work. I apologized, checked the repair history and called the technician. In the end, we replaced the phone, and he thanked me before he left.

lines.speaker: Ms. Chen
lines.text: Nice. This job involves a lot of teamwork. Tell me about a time when you worked with others to reach a goal.

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: At the community centre, our team organized a food drive. I was responsible for the schedule, so I asked each volunteer which hours suited them. We collected more food than we had planned.

lines.speaker: Ms. Chen
lines.text: Good. And what is an area you are still working to improve?

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: My spoken English is not perfect yet, especially on the phone. I practise every day, and I take notes during calls, so that I do not miss any details.

lines.speaker: Ms. Chen
lines.text: I appreciate your honesty. This position involves shifts, including some evenings and weekends. Is that a problem?

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: No, I am flexible. I can work evenings and weekends, and I can start as soon as you need me.

lines.speaker: Ms. Chen
lines.text: Excellent. Do you have any questions for me?

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: Yes. What does training look like for new employees, and who would I report to?

lines.speaker: Ms. Chen
lines.text: New employees train with an experienced colleague for the first weeks, and you would report to me. We will contact your references this week and we will be in touch soon with our decision.

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: Thank you very much for your time. I am very interested in the job.

segments.text: From the job posting: We are looking for a friendly, reliable team member. Responsibilities include helping customers, handling cash and returns, and keeping the sales floor tidy. Customer service experience is an asset. Availability for evenings and weekends is required. The ability to work in a fast-paced environment is important. To apply, send your résumé and a cover letter.
Tip: Arrive a few minutes early, bring a copy of your résumé, and prepare an example for each strength you mention. After the interview, it is polite to send a short e-mail to thank the interviewer.

scenarios.title: Filing Your Taxes
scenarios.summary: Wei asks his neighbour Elena how a first income tax return works: slips, refunds, deadlines and where to get help. It also has an excerpt from a tax agency letter.
scenarios.summaryZh: 魏向邻居埃琳娜请教第一次报税:税表、退税、截止日期和哪里可以得到帮助。另附一段税务局来信节选。
scenarios.canadaNoteZh: 在加拿大,即使收入不高也建议每年报税,很多福利和退税要靠报税才能领取。截止日期每年可能不同,请到加拿大税务局(CRA)官网核对。
verify: The yearly filing deadline: the text gives no date, only that there is a deadline and where to check it.

Free community tax clinics (CRA's volunteer program) exist, but their rules for who can use them change. The text says only that free help exists for people with simple returns and modest income, and to check the CRA website.
A T4 is the usual slip from an employer for employment income. Other slips exist. The text mentions only the T4.
A notice of assessment is sent by the CRA after the return is processed. How it is received (online or by mail) depends on the person's settings.
Whether a return is needed even with no income, and which credits a newcomer may claim, is not covered by the text.
The letter is invented for the story. How and by when an objection can be filed is not stated; check the official website.

segments.text: Wei started working in Canada last year, and now he must file his first income tax return. He asks his neighbour Elena for advice.

lines.speaker: Wei
lines.text: Elena, I got a letter about taxes. Do I really have to file a tax return?

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Almost everyone who earned money here does. Once a year, you report your income to the Canada Revenue Agency, or the CRA. Even if you do not owe anything, filing is a good idea, because many benefits and credits depend on it.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Honestly, it is not as scary as it sounds. Just do not leave it to the last minute.

lines.speaker: Wei
lines.text: What do I need to do first?

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Collect your documents. Your employer should send you a T4, a slip that shows how much you earned and how much tax was already taken from your pay. Also keep receipts for anything that may count as a deduction, for example some education costs or child care.

lines.speaker: Wei
lines.text: How do I actually file?

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Most people use tax software and file online. If your situation is simple and your income is modest, you may also get free help from a community volunteer tax clinic. Check the CRA website to see if you qualify.

lines.speaker: Wei
lines.text: And what happens after I file?

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: The CRA sends a notice of assessment, which says whether your return was accepted. If you paid more tax during the year than you needed to, you get a refund. If you paid too little, you will have a balance owing, and you must pay it.

lines.speaker: Wei
lines.text: Is there a deadline?

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Yes, there is a deadline every year, and it can change, so look at the CRA website instead of trusting me. If you file late and you owe money, you may be charged a penalty and interest.

lines.speaker: Wei
lines.text: That makes me nervous. What if I make a mistake?

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Do not worry. You can correct a return later, and the CRA is used to helping people who are new. Just be honest and keep your papers for several years, in case they have questions.

lines.speaker: Wei
lines.text: Thank you. I will gather my documents this weekend.

segments.text: From a letter of the tax agency: We have reviewed your return and issued your notice of assessment. If you disagree with our decision, you may file an objection. If you have a balance owing, please pay by the due date to avoid interest. Keep your receipts and supporting documents in case we ask to see them.

Tip: Be careful of phone calls, texts or e-mails that say you owe taxes and must pay at once, especially with gift cards or by sending money. The CRA does not work like that. If you are unsure, hang up and check the official CRA website.

scenarios.title: Calling 911
scenarios.summary: Lina's neighbour slipped on the ice and cannot get up. She calls 911, answers the dispatcher's questions and stays on the line until help arrives.
scenarios.summaryZh: 莉娜的邻居在冰上滑倒,爬不起来。她拨打 911,回答接线员的问题,并保持通话直到救援到达。
scenarios.canadaNoteZh: 紧急情况(有人受伤、起火、正在发生的犯罪)才打 911。接通后先说清楚在哪个城市和具体地址,再说发生了什么。听不懂也不要挂断,可以说 "I need an interpreter" 或慢慢重复关键词。不确定是不是紧急情况时,也可以直接问接线员。
verify: Whether a 911 dispatcher can bring in an interpreter, and for which languages, differs by service. The text only has the caller say she is not sure of the word, and does not promise an interpreter.
The dispatcher's questions (city first, then police, fire or ambulance, then address) are typical, but the order and wording differ by dispatch centre. Calgary and Alberta wording is not confirmed.
Advice not to move an injured person is general first-aid advice for a possible broken bone or neck or back injury. Confirm it fits the story's injury.
The dispatcher telling the caller to stay on the line, and to send someone to meet the ambulance, is common practice, not a rule.
Calling 911 from a cell phone: the location sent to the dispatcher may be imprecise, so giving the address is correct. The exact accuracy is not stated in the text.
Text-to-911 exists only for people registered in advance (for example people who are deaf or hard of hearing). It is not mentioned in the text on purpose.
Whether to call 911 for non-emergencies is not covered; the tip says only to use it for real emergencies.

segments.text: On a cold morning in Calgary, Lina sees her neighbour, Mr. Brown, lying on the icy sidewalk in front of his house. He says his leg hurts and he cannot stand up. Lina takes out her phone and calls 911.

lines.speaker: Dispatcher
lines.text: 911. What city are you in?

lines.speaker: Lina
lines.text: Calgary.

lines.speaker: Dispatcher
lines.text: Do you need police, fire or ambulance?

lines.speaker: Lina
lines.text: Ambulance, please. My neighbour fell on the ice and he cannot get up. I think his leg is broken.

lines.speaker: Dispatcher
lines.text: All right, I am sending help. What is the address of the emergency?

lines.speaker: Lina
lines.text: He is lying in front of the house on Maple Street, near the corner of Maple Street and Fifth Avenue. Sorry, I am not sure about the house number. I can read it to you in a moment.

lines.speaker: Dispatcher
lines.text: That is fine. Stay on the line. Is he awake and conscious? Is he breathing normally?

lines.speaker: Lina
lines.text: Yes, he is awake. He is talking to me, but he is in pain.

lines.speaker: Dispatcher
lines.text: Good. Please do not move him. Can you cover him with a coat or a blanket to keep him warm?

lines.speaker: Lina
lines.text: Yes, I can do that. I have a coat with me.

lines.speaker: Dispatcher
lines.text: Does he have any medical conditions, or take any medication that you know of?

lines.speaker: Lina
lines.text: I do not know. I will ask him. He says he takes medicine for his heart.

lines.speaker: Dispatcher
lines.text: Thank you. That helps. Now, can you read me the number on the house?

lines.speaker: Lina
lines.text: Yes, it is on the door. I can see it now.

lines.speaker: Dispatcher
lines.text: Perfect. The ambulance is on its way. Please stay with him and do not hang up. If anything changes, tell me right away.

lines.speaker: Lina
lines.text: I will. Is there anything else I should do?

lines.speaker: Dispatcher
lines.text: If you can, ask someone to wait by the road and wave to the paramedics, so they can find you quickly. When they arrive, tell them what you told me.

lines.speaker: Lina
lines.text: Understood. Thank you.

segments.text: Tip: Call 911 only in an emergency, for example when someone is badly hurt, there is a fire, or a crime is happening now. Stay calm, speak slowly, give the city and the address first, and answer the questions one at a time. Do not hang up until the dispatcher tells you that you can.

scenarios.title: At the Pharmacy
scenarios.summary: Mei picks up an antibiotic, tells the pharmacist about her allergy, asks how to take the medicine and buys cough syrup.
scenarios.summaryZh: 小美取一种抗生素,告诉药师自己的过敏情况,问清楚怎么吃药,还买了止咳糖浆。
scenarios.canadaNoteZh: 在加拿大,药师(pharmacist)会当面讲解怎么吃药,你可以随时提问,不用不好意思。取药时带上健康卡和药物保险卡(如果有)。药费能报多少取决于你的保险和所在省份。有些常见药不需要处方,可以直接在药房货架上买。
verify: How much of the drug cost insurance covers, and whether public drug coverage exists, differs by province and plan. The text says only that she pays a small part.
Health card names differ by province (in Alberta it is the Alberta Health Care card). The text uses only "health card" and does not check that a health card is asked for at a pharmacy.
Whether pharmacists in Alberta can renew a prescription is true in some provinces, but the details differ. The text has the pharmacist say that Mei can ask for a refill, without naming a rule.
Taking the antibiotic with food and finishing every pill are typical instructions, but depend on the drug. The medicine in the story is invented.
A pharmacist checking for allergies and other medicines before giving a prescription is standard practice, but the exact questions differ by pharmacy.
Over-the-counter medicine on a shelf versus behind the counter: some products are kept behind the counter in some places. The text only mentions a shelf.

segments.text: Mei has a bad throat infection, and her doctor gave her a prescription. Now she is at a pharmacy in Calgary. The pharmacist, Raj, is at the counter.

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.text: Hello. How can I help you?

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: Hi. I would like to pick up a prescription for Mei Chen, please.

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.text: Sure. Can I see your health card, please?

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: Here it is.

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.text: Thank you. One moment. Yes, I have it here. This is an antibiotic. Before I give it to you, do you have any allergies?

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: Yes, I am allergic to penicillin.

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.text: Thank you for telling me. This medicine is a different kind, so it is safe for you. Are you taking any other medicine right now?

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: No, nothing else.

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.text: Good. Take one pill in the morning and one at night, with food. Finish the whole bottle, even if you feel better after a few days. If your doctor wants you to continue, I can help you with a refill.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: I see. What if I forget to take one?

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.text: Take it as soon as you remember, but do not take a double dose. Some people feel a little sick to their stomach, and that is a common side effect. If you get a rash or trouble breathing, call your doctor or go to a hospital right away.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: Thank you. Do I need to pay?

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.text: Do you have drug insurance from your work?

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: Yes, I have a card from my job.

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.text: Great. Then you only pay a small part. I will take care of the rest with your insurance.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: Also, I have a cough. Can I get something for it?

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.text: Yes. Cough syrup is over-the-counter, so you do not need a prescription. It is on the shelf in aisle three. If you are not sure which one to choose, ask me and I can help you.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: Thank you very much for your help.

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.text: You're welcome. Feel better soon!

segments.text: On the pharmacy label: take one pill twice a day with food. Keep out of reach of children. Store in a cool, dry place.

Tip: Tell the pharmacist about all your allergies and all the medicines you take, even vitamins. Ask when and how to take the medicine, and what to do if you miss a dose. The pharmacist is a health professional, and the advice is free.

Many Canadians do not have a family doctor, and waiting times differ. The story assumes Daniel already has one.
Whether a clinic asks you to arrive early to fill in a form, and what the reception asks for, differs by clinic.

segments.text: Daniel has had headaches and has felt very tired for two weeks. He has an appointment with his family doctor, Dr. Singh, at a clinic in Calgary. First he must check in with the receptionist at the front desk, shows his health card and waits in the waiting room. Then Dr. Singh calls his name.

lines.speaker: Dr. Singh
lines.text: Daniel? Please come in. Have a seat. What brings you in today?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: For the past two weeks, I have had headaches almost every day, and I feel tired all the time.

lines.speaker: Dr. Singh
lines.text: I see. Where is the pain, and how bad is it?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: It is mostly at the front of my head. It is not terrible, but it makes it hard to concentrate at work.

lines.speaker: Dr. Singh
lines.text: Have you taken anything for it?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Only a pain reliever, a couple of times. It helped for a few hours.

lines.speaker: Dr. Singh
lines.text: How is your sleep? And do you drink a lot of coffee?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: I sleep about five hours a night, because I work late shifts. I drink about four cups of coffee a day.

lines.speaker: Dr. Singh
lines.text: That could explain a lot. Let me check your blood pressure and listen to your heart and lungs.

lines.speaker: Dr. Singh
lines.text: Everything looks normal. I would like to rule out a few other causes, so I am going to order a blood test. You can go to a lab, and I will send them the request.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Do I need to do anything to prepare?

lines.speaker: Dr. Singh
lines.text: It depends on the test, so please read the form carefully. In the meantime, try to get more sleep, drink more water and cut down on coffee. If the headaches get much worse, or you feel dizzy or confused, go to the emergency room.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Okay. When will I get the results?

lines.speaker: Dr. Singh
lines.text: My office will contact you. Please book a follow-up appointment at the front desk so we can talk about the results.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Thank you, doctor.

segments.text: Tip: Before the visit, write down your symptoms, when they started, any medicine you take and your questions. In the doctor's office, speak slowly and ask the doctor to repeat or explain anything you do not understand, for example: "Could you say that again, please?" or "What does that mean?"

segments.text: On Saturday morning, Hana is shopping at a grocery store in Calgary. She has a list and a flyer from this week. She is already in line at the cashier when she remembers that she forgot the rice.

scenarios.title: Taking the Bus
scenarios.summary: Ahmed asks a driver and a fellow passenger how to get downtown by bus and train, learns about transfers and the transit card, and gets off at the right stop.
scenarios.summaryZh: 艾哈迈德向司机和乘客打听怎么乘公交和轻轨去市中心,了解换乘和公交卡,并在正确的站下车。
scenarios.canadaNoteZh: 各城市的交通卡和付费方式不同(例如多伦多的 Presto、温哥华的 Compass、蒙特利尔的 OPUS),卡尔加里常用手机 App 或购票机买票,上车前先在官方网站或 App 看清楚。一定要看路线号码和"终点方向"。要下车时按车内的 stop 按钮或拉线。冬天路滑,提前几分钟到站台。

segments.text: Ahmed has just moved to Calgary, and today he wants to go downtown to visit a friend. He is waiting at a bus stop. A woman, Grace, is waiting next to him, and they start to talk. Later they ride the bus and the train together.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Excuse me, does this bus go downtown?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: This one goes to the train station. You can take the train from there. It runs every few minutes during the day.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: I see. Do I need a separate ticket for the train?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: No. You can change between the bus and the train with one fare, as long as you do it within the time limit. That is called a transfer.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: That is helpful. How do I pay?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Many people use a transit pass or pay with an app. If you are not sure, you can check the official website or ask the driver.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Okay. Here comes the bus. Should I sit at the front?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: You can sit anywhere, but the seats at the front are for older people and people with disabilities. Please leave them free if someone needs them.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Of course. How will I know where to get off?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: The driver will announce each stop, and you will also see it on the screen. Your station is the last stop, so you cannot miss it.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Great. Is this the right platform for the downtown train?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Yes, this one. Look at the sign on the front of the train. It should say downtown. Do you know your stop?

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: I am going to the Eighth Avenue station.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Then you will get off in about ten minutes. The doors open automatically on the train, but on a bus you have to press the stop button before your stop.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: That is good to know. Thank you so much for your help!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: You're welcome. Enjoy your day!

segments.text: Tip: Before you travel, use the transit website or app to check your route. Look at the route number and the final destination on the front of the bus, because the same number can go in two directions. Arrive a few minutes early, especially in winter. If you are not sure, ask the driver or another passenger.

segments.text: It snowed all night in Calgary. This morning Wei is shovelling the walkway in front of his house. His neighbour, Sandra, comes out to do the same, and they say hello.

lines.speaker: Sandra
lines.text: Good morning, Wei! Quite a lot of snow last night, isn't it?

lines.speaker: Wei
lines.text: Good morning, Sandra. It certainly is. I woke up and could not see the street.

lines.speaker: Sandra
lines.text: It happens every winter. How are you finding your first winter in Calgary?

lines.speaker: Wei
lines.text: Honestly, it is colder than I expected, but it is beautiful. People keep telling me it is a dry cold, so it does not feel as bad.

lines.speaker: Sandra
lines.text: That is true. And you never know here. One day it is freezing, and the next day a chinook comes and it feels like spring.

lines.speaker: Wei
lines.text: A chinook? I have heard that word. What exactly is it?

lines.speaker: Sandra
lines.text: It is a warm wind that comes over the mountains. The temperature can rise very fast, and the snow starts to melt.

lines.speaker: Wei
lines.text: Interesting. I should be careful with my shovelling, then. Maybe I will wait until the afternoon.

lines.speaker: Sandra
lines.text: Ha! Not a bad idea. Actually, if you need to borrow a shovel or a bag of salt, just ask. I have an extra one.

lines.speaker: Wei
lines.text: That is very kind of you. For now I have everything I need, but thank you for offering.

lines.speaker: Sandra
lines.text: Anytime. By the way, I am going to get a coffee at Tim Hortons later. Would you like to join me? I am buying.

lines.speaker: Wei
lines.text: Thanks for asking, but I have to be at work in an hour. Maybe another time?

lines.speaker: Sandra
lines.text: Sure, no problem. Oh, and a quick tip: the garbage and recycling bins go out on different days. There is a schedule on the city website.

lines.speaker: Wei
lines.text: Thanks, I will check it. I am still learning how everything works here.

lines.speaker: Sandra
lines.text: You'll get used to it. Well, I'd better get back to shovelling. Stay warm!

lines.speaker: Wei
lines.text: You too. Have a great day!

segments.text: Tip: Small talk is short and friendly. Common topics are the weather, the weekend, sports and the neighbourhood. Good ways to start are "Nice weather today, isn't it?" or "How is your day going?" You do not have to give personal details, and it is polite to end the chat with a smile and a phrase such as "Have a good one!"

segments.text: Nadia has just started a new job in Calgary, and her employer asked for her Social Insurance Number, or SIN. She also needs a health card. She goes to a Service Canada office and speaks to a clerk, Mr. Lee.

lines.speaker: Mr. Lee
lines.text: Hello. How can I help you today?

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: Hello. I recently moved here and I have a work permit. I need a Social Insurance Number, and I also want to know about a health card.

lines.speaker: Mr. Lee
lines.text: I can help with the SIN. A health card is handled by the province, but I can tell you in general what to do. Let's start with the SIN. Do you have your original documents with you?

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: I have my passport and my work permit.

lines.speaker: Mr. Lee
lines.text: Good. Those are your proof of identity and your status in Canada. I will check that they are valid. May I see them, please?

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: Here you go.

lines.speaker: Mr. Lee
lines.text: Thank you. I will also need your current address and your date of birth. Please fill in this form.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: Done. Is that enough?

lines.speaker: Mr. Lee
lines.text: Yes. Your SIN will be given to you in writing, and you should keep that paper in a safe place. Please do not share the number unless it is necessary, for example with your employer for payroll or for tax reporting.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: Understood. What about the health card?

lines.speaker: Mr. Lee
lines.text: For that, you have to apply with the province. Usually you complete an application and show documents that prove who you are, that you live in the province, and that you are allowed to stay in Canada. Check the provincial government website for the exact steps.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: Is there a waiting period before the card starts to work?

lines.speaker: Mr. Lee
lines.text: In some provinces there is, but it depends on your situation. Ask when you apply, and find out what to do about medical care while you wait. Some people buy private insurance for that time.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: That is very useful. Where should I go to apply?

lines.speaker: Mr. Lee
lines.text: The provincial website will tell you the nearest office. You may also be able to do part of it online. And remember to update your address with them whenever you move.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: I will. Thank you for all your help.

lines.speaker: Mr. Lee
lines.text: You're welcome. Good luck with your new job!

segments.text: Checklist for the visit: original passport and work or study permit (not photocopies), proof of your address, a pen, and a list of your questions. Take a number or ticket when you arrive, and wait until it is called.

Tip: Your SIN is private. Keep it in a safe place, do not carry the paper in your wallet, and do not give it to anyone who calls or writes to you without a good reason. Employers need it for payroll, and you will need it for your taxes. Your health card is also private, and you should show it only to the clinic or hospital.
